messages:
maria: quick heads-up, I ran a small KV-cache benchmarking sweep across us-east (H100) and eu-west (A100) with our new nonblocking-evict shim. results look...interesting. hitrate by seqlen buckets + p50/p95/p99 latency diverge more than i expected.

maria: test config: --model r-instruct-30b --quant q4_0 --batch 16 --prefetch-window 8 --evict=strict_clock --cache-size 20GB --trace kv,traces --region us-east/eu-west

maria: short summary in numbers (slen buckets = [<=64, 65-256, 257-1024]):
```
region,kernel,slen_bucket,hitrate,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,thru_tok/s
us-east,H100,fused-attn,<=64,94%,12,26,42,1200
us-east,H100,fused-attn,65-256,88%,18,45,110,980
us-east,H100,fused-attn,257-1024,61%,40,120,310,420
eu-west,A100,gemm-kernel,<=64,92%,14,30,55,1050
eu-west,A100,gemm-kernel,65-256,80%,22,60,220,740
eu-west,A100,gemm-kernel,257-1024,48%,55,200,560,260
```

maria: notes:
- hitrate drop for long sequences is the main p99 driver. H100 holds up better on mid buckets; A100 falls off earlier.
- eviction policy `strict_clock` is deterministic but causes churn when slen mixes hit cache capacity; p99 spikes when paging occurs concurrently across many requests.
- prefetch window 8 helps p50 but increases p99 in eu-west when combined with the gemm kernel because paging I/O blocks kernel switches.

sam: nice, thanks. can you upload the raw traces/plots? i'd like the per-kernel timeline to see if cache eviction correlates exactly with kernel swaps. also, what was the CPU-side paging pressure?

maria: uploaded to /shared/bench/2003456789/traces.tar.gz (small). cpu paging was low on H100 hosts, higher on A100 hosts during high-slen tail. attached a quick timeline (png) in the folder.

jen: quick thought: try `evict=probabilistic` with alpha=0.6 and reduce prefetch-window->4 for eu-west A100. that reduces simultaneous page-ins and smooths p99 in our past runs. also consider increasing kv.cache.eviction_grace=150ms so we avoid thrashing on near-simultaneous evict/insert cycles.

maria: good idea. i pushed a control run with those changes: --evict=probabilistic --evict-alpha=0.6 --prefetch-window 4 --eviction-grace 150ms. early numbers look like:
```
region,kernel,slen_bucket,hitrate,p99_ms
eu-west,A100,257-1024,60%,320 (was 560)
us-east,H100,257-1024,66%,280 (was 310)
```

sam: that's promising. can you also try the same on an H100 in eu-west (we have a small pool) to separate region vs hw effects? if hw is primary, we should prefer fused-attn kernels in us-east routing and gemm fallback for low-cost bursts in eu-west.

prefetch-bot: prefetcher metrics: average in-flight prefetches dropped from 18->6 after window=4, kv cache miss burst rate dropped ~38%.

maria: will run the H100 eu-west job tomorrow and post results. for next steps: 1) rerun H100 eu-west with probabilistic/alpha=0.6 + prefetch=4, 2) generate stacked p99 waterfall by request arrival time, 3) add a lightweight canary to route 10% of traffic to fused-attn on eu-west to measure live delta.

jen: agree. if canary looks good we can make routing policy region-aware + kernel-preference hints. also let's add a small eval prompt set (length mix) to detect quality regressions from quantization while we tune cache parameters.

sam: thanks — let's reconvene after the H100 eu-west run. :thumbsup:
